title: EC2 Instance State Changes

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudtrail` events with `(eventName="RunInstances" OR eventName="TerminateInstances" OR eventName="StopInstances" OR eventName="StartInstances")` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.6 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `(eventName="RunInstances" OR eventName="TerminateInstances" OR eventName="StopInstances" OR eventName="StartInstances")`. Confirm UC-4.1.6 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" (eventName="RunInstances" OR eventName="TerminateInstances" OR eventName="StopInstances" OR eventName="StartInstances")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.6_ec2_instance_state_chang_6"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.1.6 — EC2 Instance State Changes: queries AWS `aws:cloudtrail` for `RunInstances` (+3 related API operations) and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On AWS, `RunInstances` activity for 'EC2 Instance State Changes' is a high-signal control-plane change that should match approved change records and privileged-access monitoring. UC-4.1.6 drives medium-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Ingest CloudTrail via the Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`) using the S3/SQS input from the organization trail. Alert on `TerminateInstances` where `requestParameters.instancesSet.items{}.instanceId` matches production-tagged instances from a `prod_instances` lookup. Suppress alerts during Auto Scaling scale-in events by checking `userIdentity.invokedBy=autoscaling.amazonaws.com`.
visualization: Table (timeline), Bar chart (events by type per day), Line chart (instance count trending).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  where All_Changes.object_category="instance" OR match(All_Changes.object, "(?i)ec2:|i-[0-9a-f]{8,17}")
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object All_Changes.action span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Change (All_Changes): for CloudTrail management events mapped to CIM. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Auto Scaling, patch cycles, and CI workers that start/stop or replace instances you expect in non-prod or blue/green.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest CloudTrail via the Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`) using the S3/SQS input from the organization trail. Alert on `TerminateInstances` where `requestParameters.instancesSet.items{}.instanceId` matches production-tagged instances from a `prod_instances` lookup. Suppress alerts during Auto Scaling scale-in events by checking `userIdentity.invokedBy=autoscaling.amazonaws.com`.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" (eventName="RunInstances" OR eventName="TerminateInstances" OR eventName="StopInstances" OR eventName="StartInstances")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.6_ec2_instance_state_chang_6"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect ec2 instance state changes. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_6_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (timeline), Bar chart (events by type per day), Line chart (instance count trending)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of ec2 instance state changes so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
